ai-073.cap:
Turn this on now. Five presses can call for help 🆘
How to set up Emergency SOS and emergency contacts on iPhone

1. Open Settings and tap Emergency SOS
2. Turn on Call with 5 Presses (and Call with Hold and Release if you want it)
3. Then rapidly pressing the side button five times starts a countdown to call emergency services
4. Open the Health app, tap your picture, then Medical ID. Tap Get Started or Edit and add your emergency contacts
5. Scroll down and turn on Show When Locked and Emergency Call

After an emergency call ends, your iPhone texts your emergency contacts with your location (if available), unless you cancel. Checked on Apple's iOS 26 and iOS 27 guides; menus can change, so check your phone's version. The shortcut differs in some countries. If you call by accident, stay on the line and tell them you're OK. Only for real emergencies.

ai-074.cap:
Stop guessing. One number tells you when your money doubles ⏳
Rule of 72: how long it takes your money to double

1. Take 72
2. Divide it by the yearly rate of return (just the number: 9, not 0.09)
3. The answer is about how many years it takes to double
4. At 9%: 72 ÷ 9 = about 8 years (Investor.gov's own example)
5. At 4%: 72 ÷ 4 = about 18 years

It's a quick estimate, not a promise. Real returns change from year to year, and Investor.gov says all investments involve some degree of risk. The rates here are examples. This is general info, not financial advice.

wd-106.t: If you get this text, don't tap it: fake delivery text red flags
wd-106.cap:
If you get this text, don't tap it: fake delivery text red flags
A fake "your package couldn't be delivered" text with a tiny fee is one of the most common scam texts. Learn 4 red flags once, and you can check any text in seconds.

1. It rushes or threatens you ("pay today or it goes back")
2. A link you didn't ask for
3. An odd number or sender
4. It wants a code or card number

Spot one? Don't tap. Check your order in the store's or carrier's own app (typed yourself). Forward the text to 7726 (free on most US carriers), then delete it. Already tapped and paid? Call the number on the back of your card.
